## Source: amazon-inspector (82a1f2ebbd0f8423c7e02c1a9b0571cec02bd6d343b88583f6a85dd06a056a99)
setup.py overrides the install command to collect the installer's hostname and resolved local IP address and POST them as JSON to the hardcoded URL https://webhook.site/17a7df2e-3d56-4c5a-b7a9-9a95fe58a533 during `pip install`, tagged with the package name and version. The beacon fires unconditionally at install time with no user disclosure or opt-out, and the package itself provides no documented functionality — the shipped code is a proof-of-concept beacon with placeholder author metadata. The exfiltrated data is limited to host identifiers (hostname, IP) rather than credentials, but the install-time network callback to a third-party collector enables correlation of installations with the operator of the webhook endpoint.

## Source: kam193 (2cd8f99409a87f01743f65f381fefa800176a29d47d6119743ae2bd0ce1f7583)
Installing the package or importing the module exfiltrates basic information about the host, and the package has no other purpose.
